title: Berlin moves to block Cosco–Zippel; Germany's draft Investment Screening Act
summary: Germany prepares to prohibit Cosco's 80 per cent stake in Hamburg logistics firm Zippel and circulates a draft Investment Screening Act, alongside an Italian golden power decree on Pirelli, a CFIUS mitigation agreement for BitFuFu, a Canadian national-security review of a lithium deal and Mexico's Senate passing a screening reform.
script:
Good morning. This is FDI Daily for Friday, the 2nd of October. Today, Berlin moves towards blocking a Chinese takeover in German logistics and puts a tougher screening law on the table. We also have an Italian golden power decree, a CFIUS mitigation agreement, a Canadian national-security review of a lithium deal, and a new screening regime taking shape in Mexico.

We start in Germany. According to Handelsblatt, followed by Reuters on Tuesday the 29th of September, the federal government intends to prohibit the acquisition of an eighty per cent stake in Konrad Zippel Spedition by the Chinese state-owned shipping group Cosco. Zippel is a Hamburg logistics group running hinterland container transport for the ports of Hamburg and Bremerhaven. The review sits with the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy under the Foreign Trade and Payments Act and Ordinance.

Reuters quotes an internal government memo warning that the resulting strategic dependencies could be used as leverage in the event of political upheavals. The review reportedly focused on Zippel's software systems and whether it handles sensitive data. Handelsblatt adds a defence dimension. Zippel supports Bundeswehr and NATO logistics, and the documents warn that China-influenced parts of European transport infrastructure might not be fully available in a conflict or crisis. The Foreign Office and the Defence Ministry are reported to back a prohibition. The procedural history is notable. The Federal Cartel Office cleared the deal on competition grounds in February. According to Handelsblatt, the government said in May that no veto was possible because Zippel was not classed as critical infrastructure. It is now reconsidering, with reference to the new critical infrastructure umbrella law.

At the government press conference on Wednesday the 30th, a ministry spokesperson confirmed only that the acquisition is under investment review, and declined to say more. Cosco says it cannot comment before a final decision from Berlin. Zippel says it has taken note and business continues as normal. No formal prohibition has been issued. For context, Cosco already holds the minority stake in a Hamburg container terminal that Berlin allowed in 2023.

Now to deal watch.

In Rome, the Council of Ministers on the 24th of September exercised golden powers over a defence co-development agreement between Pirelli and ABET High Tech Solutions. Both companies are Italian. The agreement, announced on the 5th of August, covers remote-controlled electric ground vehicles for rescue in extreme terrain. The prime ministerial decree, notified on the 28th, finds both companies' defence activities and the agreement to be of strategic importance for the defence system. It imposes technical and organisational prescriptions to protect intellectual property, know-how, products and strategic data, and to keep research and development continuous and up to standard. The detailed terms are not public. Note that this is a cooperation agreement, not an acquisition.

In Washington, CFIUS cleared BitFuFu's acquisition of fifty-one per cent of Uni-Titan on the 28th of September, subject to a national security agreement. BitFuFu is headquartered in Singapore. Uni-Titan operates a fifty-one megawatt bitcoin mining facility in Oklahoma. The Department of Homeland Security and the Treasury are the monitoring agencies. According to the company's announcement, the agreement restricts the site to specified crypto mining operations, limits deployment of certain advanced computing hardware, and subjects facility improvements and equipment changes to government oversight. The filing was notified in December 2025, so this was a review of around nine months.

In Ottawa, Lithium Chile announced on the 29th of September that Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada has notified China Union Holdings that it will conduct a formal review, under section 25 of the Investment Canada Act, of its proposed acquisition of Argentum Lithium. Argentum holds the Arizaro lithium project in Argentina. China Union Holdings is reviewing the order and has not yet said how it will respond. No grounds have been disclosed.

On to the regime roundup, starting in Berlin again. The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy has sent an eighty-six page draft Investment Screening Act to the other ministries. It was reported by Handelsblatt and the dts agency on the 1st of October. The draft states that the geopolitical security situation and the risks to Germany's national and economic security have intensified considerably, and names Chinese influence as a particular concern. Reported points include screening of stakes in listed companies from fifteen per cent, a fresh review when a foreign investor moves to full control, and the end of the exemption for Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. Reports differ on EU investors. The dts agency says screening remains limited to non-EU investors, while Handelsblatt reports EU investors could be caught in critical infrastructure. No cabinet date has been set. It comes ahead of the revised EU Screening Regulation, which applies from January 2028.

Further afield, to Mexico. On the 30th of September the Senate passed, by sixty-five votes to thirty, a reform of the Foreign Investment Law that creates a national security review. A new title in the law covers foreign acquisitions of more than forty-nine per cent of companies in strategic sectors. The National Foreign Investment Commission grows from ten to thirteen member ministries, adding Defence, the Navy and Security and Citizen Protection. Tacit approval is abolished for national security cases. Fines reach two hundred thousand times the daily reference unit, around twenty-three point four million pesos. The bill now goes to the Chamber of Deputies.

In the wider world. G20 trade ministers meeting in Milwaukee failed to agree on industrial overcapacity or forced labour in supply chains. The US Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, said current trade remedies are inadequate. The United States has overcapacity investigations open into sixteen economies, including China, the EU, Japan and India.

China's Commerce Ministry has warned it will resolutely respond to any discriminatory EU measures against Chinese companies. This follows reports that France and Germany are pushing Brussels for a faster and tougher trade defence tool against China.

The US Treasury designated more than two dozen entities and two individuals on the 1st of October in its Iran campaign. The targets are in automotive, rail, metals and shadow banking, with designees in Hong Kong, the UAE, Turkey, Indonesia and Germany. Treasury also issued sector determinations that widen secondary sanctions risk.

And according to the Financial Times, Sycamore Partners is in advanced talks to sell Boots to the Canadian Weston family's Wittington Investments for around nine billion dollars. A deal could come as soon as next week.

The watch list. Handelsblatt reports that a formal decision on Cosco and Zippel could come as early as next week. On Monday the 5th of October, the Swiss consultation on the Investment Screening Ordinance, which implements the new Investment Screening Act, closes. The 4th of November is the provisional deadline in the Commission's in-depth Foreign Subsidies Regulation review of JD.com's acquisition of Ceconomy, where commitments are on the table. On the 10th of November, the UK Supreme Court hears LetterOne's appeal against the Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster. It is the first National Security and Investment Act case at that level, and the question is whether the forced sale of Upp required market-value compensation under Article 1 of the First Protocol. And Japan's amended Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act rules take effect from the 4th of January next year.

That's FDI Daily for this Friday. Have a good weekend.

items.headline: Germany intends to prohibit Cosco's 80 per cent stake in Zippel
items.what_was_said: Handelsblatt and Reuters (29 Sep 2026) report Berlin intends to prohibit Cosco's acquisition of 80 per cent of Hamburg logistics firm Konrad Zippel Spedition. A memo warns of strategic dependencies usable as leverage, and the review focused on software systems and sensitive data. Bundeswehr and NATO logistics are cited, and the Federal Cartel Office cleared the deal in February. The BMWE confirmed on 30 Sep only that an investment review is under way. No formal prohibition yet; Handelsblatt says a decision could come next week.

deal.target: Konrad Zippel Spedition (80 per cent stake)
deal.authority: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE)
deal.detail: Investment review under AWG/AWV; government reportedly intends to prohibit. Reported grounds: strategic dependencies usable as leverage in political upheaval; software systems and sensitive data; Bundeswehr/NATO logistics; transport infrastructure availability in crisis. Antitrust clearance February 2026. No formal decision as of 2 Oct 2026.

items.headline: Italy imposes golden power prescriptions on Pirelli–ABET HTS defence agreement
items.what_was_said: On 24 Sep 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a golden power decree, notified 28 Sep, on Pirelli's co-development agreement with ABET High Tech Solutions for remote-controlled electric rescue ground vehicles. It finds the defence activities strategically important and imposes techno-organisational prescriptions protecting IP, know-how, products, strategic data and R&D continuity.

deal.acquirer: Pirelli & C. S.p.A. (co-development agreement with ABET High Tech Solutions S.r.l.)
deal.target: ABET High Tech Solutions S.r.l. / Pirelli defence activities (cooperation agreement, not an acquisition)
deal.authority: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (golden power, DL 21/2012)
deal.detail: Techno-organisational prescriptions to safeguard industrial property, know-how, products and strategic data and ensure continuity and standards of R&D; detailed terms not disclosed.

items.headline: CFIUS clears BitFuFu's stake in Oklahoma bitcoin miner under national security agreement
items.what_was_said: CFIUS cleared Singapore-headquartered BitFuFu's acquisition of 51 per cent of Uni-Titan, operator of a 51 MW Oklahoma bitcoin mining facility, on 28 Sep 2026 under a national security agreement monitored by DHS and Treasury. The NSA restricts the site to specified crypto mining, limits certain advanced computing hardware and subjects facility changes to oversight. Notified December 2025.

deal.authority: CFIUS (DHS and Treasury as monitoring agencies)
deal.detail: National security agreement: use restricted to specified crypto mining operations; limits on certain advanced computing hardware; government oversight of improvements and equipment changes; ongoing compliance framework.

items.headline: Canada orders formal ICA review of China Union Holdings' Arizaro lithium deal
items.what_was_said: Lithium Chile announced on 29 Sep 2026 that ISED notified China Union Holdings of a formal review under section 25 of the Investment Canada Act of its proposed acquisition of Argentum Lithium, holder of the Arizaro lithium project in Argentina. CUH is reviewing the order; no grounds disclosed.

deal.target: Argentum Lithium S.A. (Arizaro lithium project; linked to Lithium Chile Inc.)
deal.authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (Investment Canada Act)
deal.detail: Formal review ordered under section 25 of the Investment Canada Act; grounds not disclosed; acquirer reviewing the order.

items.headline: Germany's draft Investment Screening Act enters inter-ministerial consultation
items.what_was_said: BMWE sent an 86-page draft Investment Screening Act to other ministries (reported 1 Oct 2026). It cites a considerably worsened security situation and targets Chinese influence. Reported points: listed-company stakes screened from 15 per cent, re-review on full takeover, EFTA states lose exemption. Reports differ on screening EU investors. No cabinet date.

items.headline: Mexican Senate passes national security review reform of Foreign Investment Law
items.what_was_said: Senate passed 65–30 on 30 Sep 2026 a reform adding a national security title to the Foreign Investment Law, covering acquisitions above 49 per cent in strategic sectors. CNIE expands from 10 to 13 ministries, adding Defence, Navy and Security. Tacit approval is abolished for security cases, with fines up to 200,000 UMA, about MXN 23.4m. Goes to the Chamber of Deputies.

items.what_was_said: G20 trade ministers in Milwaukee (1–2 Oct 2026) failed to agree on industrial overcapacity or forced labour; Greer called trade remedies inadequate; US has overcapacity investigations into 16 economies.

items.headline: China warns EU over discriminatory measures as France and Germany push tougher tool
